newsitem.title: USA: SEC fines Janus Capital Corp., fund manager.
newsitem.headline: SEC fines Janus Capital Corp., fund manager.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission Monday fined Janus Capital Corp. and a portfolio fund manager a total of $41,000 for allegedly violating federal investment laws.

Janus Capital, a Denver-based investment adviser to the Janus family of mutual funds, and fund manager Ronald Speaker accepted the sanctions without admitting or denying the administrative claim, the SEC said.

Speaker, who works for Janus Capital and manages the Janus Investment and Janus Flexible Income Funds, breached his fiduciary duty by taking advantage of trading opportunities that his funds could have taken, the SEC said.
On Jan. 12, 1993, he bought $10 million worth of Time Warner debentures for his own account and sold them the same day at a $16,000 profit, the SEC said.
Janus was given a censure, or official reprimand, and fined $25,000 for allegedly failing to supervise Speaker's transactions, the agency said.
The SEC ordered Speaker to cease and desist from future violations of federal antifraud laws, to pay a $16,000 penalty and pay back his $16,000 profit along with $5,199 in interest.
He also was suspended from the securities business for 90 days and was barred from trading in most securities for three years.
